Thanks a lot!! That worked perfectly!!

I would only like to report a strange thing. I had a problem with '_' changing to '<-', so I added the following line to vimrc:

let R_assign_map = 0

However this was changing every "0" to "<-". Zero was being interpreted as a character. To solve the problem I added the following line to vimrc:

let R_assingn_map = "^"

That was an uggly solution, but it worked. But it only worked because I don't use "^" in my code.

If I may, I would only suggest that NvimR don't make this assignment for default.

Thanks again!

messages.body_plain:
When you do

let R_assign_map = 0

Nvim-R understands that you want to convert "0" into " <- ". To disable the assign map, you should put in your vimrc:

let R_assign = 0

Any suggestions?
Keith

I'm using Vim 7.4.1831, and it works here.

It might be a markdown plugin or a specific configuration in your vimrc, after/ftplugin/rmd.vim or somewhere else. Could you please try with a minimal vimrc like this:

set nocompatible
call plug#begin('~/.config/nvim/plugged')
Plug 'jalvesaq/Nvim-R'
call plug#end()
filetype plugin indent on
syntax on
let R_tmux_split = 1

Of course, you have to replace lines 2, 3 and 4 if you do not use vim-plug. I will release a new version of Nvim-R soon, but I think no change since 0.9.3 is relevant for this issue.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jakson!

I'm trying to customize a hotkey without success.

map <silent> <LocalLeader>hh :call g:SendCmdToR("render('input.Rmd','ioslides_presentation')")

Where is the error?

Thank's!
messages.body_snippet:
Hi Jakson!

messages.subject: Re: Customizing hotkey!
messages.subject_clean: Customizing hotkey!
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ivan,

The problems are:
In this case, it is better to restrict the command to Normal mode: nmap
The name of the file should be dynamically defined: expand("%")
The final carriage return is missing: <CR>
So, try this:

nmap <silent> <LocalLeader>hh :call g:SendCmdToR("render('".expand("%")."','ioslides_presentation')")<CR>

Best,

Jakson

messages.subject_clean: Sent the codes from two R files into one R console
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jeff,

You can start R from one R file and then send code to the same R console from all R files that you open in Vim. You may use :e or :tabnew or :split to start editing another file.

Best,

Jakson
